perspectives.summary: Renewable energy is a viable option

representative_posts.author: bobmarleylives.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: For every data center built the owners should be required to build a series of renewable energy plants running on wind and solar, that generate and store enough power for their needs plus all homes and industries connected to the local grid.

representative_posts.author: lovenuclear.com
representative_posts.text: 3/14 A mix of renewables and batteries (for daily peaks) alongside nuclear (for firm, low-carbon electricity) can provide a resilient path to zero-emissions electricity. Every technology needs a plan for outages and climate risks.

representative_posts.author: pdcityhall.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Zachidniak: How are you going to explore renewable ? Bell: Complicated topic but there are many things we're evaluating. The Federal Govt has shown interest in fuel cells & there are grants potentially for them. But fuel cells produce a low voltage so it would be good if they are close by #yqrcc

representative_posts.author: fwmarkc.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: wind energy to power a wasteful data centre instead of wind to power homes, hospitals, schools, and other essential public infrastructure. Wind power should go towards reducing Nova Scotia's use of fossil fuels, not to power wasteful private data centres that provide no public good.

representative_posts.author: actupper.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: *Pulls out the powerpoint about co-located magnesium fuel recycling again* But seriously, adopting tech which allow renewables deployments to profitably capture their generation in a dense storable energy carrier (like a fuel) could allow renewable deployments to waaay outrun grid constraints.

representative_posts.author: lovenuclear.com
representative_posts.text: 10/14 Relying 100% on renewables and BESS locks a country into a permanent, multi-billion-dollar mining, manufacturing, and landfill/recycling treadmill - rebuilding the entire national energy fleet potentially 3 to 5 times over the lifespan of a single nuclear plant.

representative_posts.author: pdcityhall.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Turnbull: To clarify, the question was about designs that are established & my question is about potential to shift to renewable. Bell: The designs have been completed. So no. But as we refresh infrastructure, we can look at fuel cells. #yqrcc

representative_posts.author: energysolutions.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Yesterday's PJM grid: ⚡️ 2.16M MW total load! Good news – nearly half (43.1%) was carbon-free! ☀️💨 Still, a significant 56.9% relied on traditional sources. Let's keep pushing for cleaner energy! 🌎 #PJM #GridMix #RenewableEnergy

representative_posts.author: energy-de.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Today's ⚡️ power generation in Germany (as of 19:30 CEST) 🌿 Renewable: 60.3% (gen.), 63.2% (load); Imports: 1.9% 💨 Wind: 40.0%, ⛰️ Coal: 19.5%, 🔥 Gas: 15.9%, 🌞 Solar: 9.3%, 🍃 Biomass: 8.2%, 🌊 Hydropower: 2.6%, ♻️ Waste: 2.3%, ⚡️ Others: 1.9% 🌿 Next 24h renewable forecast: 65.5%

perspectives.title: Wind Energy

representative_posts.author: isaiahbishop.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Offshore wind is one of those things we couldve been doing but kind of let drag. And weirdly, almost certainly for the wrong reasons, the provincial govt has been all over it

representative_posts.author: npilon.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I’ve tried to work out why we’ve let offshore wind (and really onshore) drag so much - noted that Newfoundland had actually had a ban in place! There’s some circumstantial evidence the Feds were discouraging wind out here out of fear it would undercut big hydro projects.

representative_posts.author: npilon.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: But there’s also an inexplicable stagnation in onshore wind projects, where that was all sorted out ages ago.

representative_posts.author: mattyv.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Victoria needs this really badly. Sunny and windy weekend and we still sat at 50% fossil energy for much of the day. Glad to see an ABC wind energy article without false balance for a change

representative_posts.author: stockfttp.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: If you look back at last yr well over 4/5ths of GB curtailment was N of that boundary almost all of the rest above B6 Despite Eng producing the most wind power it barely curtails Regulator 'saved' consumers pennies not building grid while an obvious curtailment problem was created

representative_posts.author: lightbucket.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: I guess it's fair to say the B4 boundary is a bottleneck for wind built to the north of it. I'm assembling a mega-thread to try and understand this, the conclusion I'm reaching is that forgoing a spatial energy plan to go for "connect-and-manage" was the fundamental, and expensive, mistake here.

representative_posts.author: pugetstormwatch.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Here's your reason for the short return of "False Summer." Anomalously strong ridging centered in a favorable locations to bring strong offshore flow to Western Washington. Strong east winds = higher temperatures. #wawx
